title: Precept settings
description: Settings for a Precept test suite: precept.json beside the test binary and the precept.{environment}.json overlays next to it. Generated from Precept's own settings classes. Sections and keys this schema does not name are allowed everywhere — a suite's own settings sections are as valid here as Precept's.

$schema.description: The schema this file is validated against. Read by editors, and by nothing in Precept.

Api.description: HTTP API settings, bound from the Api section of precept.json.

BaseUrl.description: Base address that relative request paths are resolved against.

LogPayloads.description: Attach full request and response bodies to the test log.

ArtifactDirectory.description: Directory for run artifacts, relative to the test binary unless rooted.

PollIntervalMilliseconds.description: How long to wait between attempts, in milliseconds.

TimeoutMilliseconds.description: How long a waiting assertion keeps re-reading its value, in milliseconds.

ConnectionStrings.description: Named database connection strings for the data module.

DefaultRetries.description: How many times a failing test is rerun when it has no explicit RetryAttribute. 0 — the default — reruns nothing; 2 means a test may run three times in all.

DefaultTimeoutMilliseconds.description: Default per-test timeout in milliseconds; 0 disables the default timeout.

Environment.description: Name of the environment under test, used to pick the settings overlay file.

Filter.description: Tests that this run pretends do not exist. See PreceptFilterSettings.

Exclude.description: Remove tests matching this expression, whatever Include says.

Include.description: Run only tests matching this expression. Empty runs everything.

Grpc.description: gRPC settings, bound from the Grpc section of precept.json.

Address.description: Default server address, for example https://localhost:5001.

AllowInsecure.description: Allow HTTP/2 without TLS. Needed for plaintext gRPC endpoints in test environments.

DeadlineMilliseconds.description: Default deadline applied to calls that do not set one, in milliseconds.

LogMessages.description: Record request and response messages in the test log.

MaxReceiveMessageSize.description: Largest response message accepted, in bytes.

IsContinuousIntegration.description: Whether this run is on a build agent. Detected from the variables the common CI systems set, and overridable like any other setting — PRECEPT_ISCONTINUOUSINTEGRATION=true makes a developer's run behave as a CI one for the evening, without a file to edit and revert.

MaxParallelism.description: How many units of work may be in flight at once, where a unit is whatever ParallelScope says it is. Defaults to the processor count. A run cannot exceed the number of units it actually has, so this is a ceiling and not a target.

ParallelScope.description: Whether a class or a single test is one unit of parallel work. Defaults to the class.

Reporting.description: Settings for the reporting pipeline. Each reporter's own settings live in a subsection of the same Reporting block and are bound separately — see PreceptReportingSettings.

AzureDevOps.description: Azure DevOps reporting, bound from Reporting:AzureDevOps in precept.json.

ApiVersion.description: REST API version the calls ask for.

AttachArtifacts.description: Upload each failed test's captured files as attachments of its result.

BatchSize.description: How many results are sent per call. Results are batched so that a thousand-scenario suite costs about ten requests rather than a thousand.

BuildId.description: Build the run is associated with, so it appears on that build's Tests tab.

CiOnly.description: File results only from a build agent, which is the default: a test run belongs to a pipeline, and results a developer produced while writing a scenario are not the ones a test plan should show as its latest. Set it to false — or Reporting:CiOnly, for every reporter at once — to file from your own machine.

Enabled.description: Whether to create a test run at all.

MaxAttachmentBytes.description: Largest artifact uploaded, in bytes. Azure DevOps itself caps an attachment at 100 MB.

OnlyMappedTests.description: Report only tests that name a Test Case work item, in a TestCaseTagPrefix tag or through TestCaseTitlePattern. Off by default: an unmapped test still belongs in the run, it just is not linked to a work item.

PersonalAccessToken.description: A personal access token with Test Management (read & write).

Project.description: The team project the test run belongs to.

RunBy.description: Who the run and its results are attributed to — Azure DevOps shows it as Run by. Defaults to whoever the token belongs to: your own account for a personal access token, and the build service identity from a pipeline.

RunName.description: Name of the test run. Defaults to the assembly name and the environment.

TestCaseTagPrefix.description: Tag prefix that names the Test Case work item a scenario covers: @tc:41207 files this test's result against work item 41207. Set it to null or empty to read ids from the title only.

TestCaseTitlePattern.description: Pattern that reads the Test Case work item out of the test's title, so a suite can carry its ids where they are already visible — Scenario: [41207] A customer checks out — rather than in a tag per scenario.

TestPlanId.description: Test plan the run is filed under, when the results belong to one.

TestSuiteId.description: Suite within TestPlanId whose points the results are filed against. Optional: left unset, every point the plan has for a test case is filed, which is what a plan with one suite per feature means.

TimeoutSeconds.description: How long any single call may take, in seconds.

CiOnly.description: Overrides where every reporter runs, whatever each one says for itself: true confines the lot to a build agent, false lets the lot run anywhere. Unset — the default — each reporter decides, and the three shipped ones are CI-only.

Enabled.description: Turns the whole pipeline off. Nothing is constructed and no queue is started, which is what an overlay wants when a developer's local run should not reach a shared dashboard.

MaxFailures.description: How many times one reporter may throw before it is dropped for the rest of the run. A destination that is down should cost one message, not one per test.

MaxTrackedFailures.description: How many failed tests Failures carries. Zero keeps none; Failed is the real count either way.

QueueCapacity.description: How many events may be waiting for one reporter before further ones are dropped.

ReportPortal.description: ReportPortal reporting, bound from Reporting:ReportPortal in precept.json.

ApiKey.description: The API key of the account the launch is reported under.

AttachArtifacts.description: Upload screenshots, traces and other captured files as attachments.

AttachOnSuccess.description: Attach artifacts of passing tests too, rather than only of failures.

Attributes.description: Attributes put on the launch. The environment is added automatically.

CiOnly.description: Report only from a build agent, which is the default: a launch belongs to a pipeline, and a developer's machine has neither the API key nor a reason to add runs to the project's statistics. Set it to false — or Reporting:CiOnly, for every reporter at once — to report from your own machine.

Description.description: Description shown on the launch. Defaults to a line naming the environment.

Enabled.description: Whether to report to ReportPortal at all.

Endpoint.description: Base address of the ReportPortal instance, without the /api path.

LaunchMode.description: DEFAULT for a launch everyone sees, DEBUG for one kept out of the project's statistics — which is what a run from a developer's machine usually wants.

LaunchName.description: Name of the launch. Defaults to the test assembly's name.

LogMessages.description: Send the lines a test logged as log entries against its item.

MaxAttachmentBytes.description: Largest artifact uploaded, in bytes. A Playwright trace of a long scenario runs to tens of megabytes and is rarely what anyone opens from a dashboard.

Project.description: The ReportPortal project the launch belongs to.

ReportCategoriesAsAttributes.description: Report each test's category tags as attributes of its test item.

Rerun.description: Report this launch as a rerun, so ReportPortal merges it into the previous one.

RerunOf.description: Name or UUID of the launch being rerun, when Rerun is set.

TimeoutSeconds.description: How long any single call may take, in seconds.

ShutdownTimeoutSeconds.description: How long the run waits, after the last test, for reporters to finish sending. Whatever is still queued when it expires is abandoned and reported as abandoned.

Teams.description: Teams reporting, bound from Reporting:Teams in precept.json.

CiOnly.description: Post only from a build agent, which is the default: a channel wants to hear about the pipeline's runs, not about every run a developer starts while working on a scenario. Set it to false — or Reporting:CiOnly, for every reporter at once — to post from your own machine.

Facts.description: Extra rows for the card's fact list — a build number, a branch, a release. Values usually come from CI through PRECEPT_REPORTING__TEAMS__FACTS__BUILD.

ImageAltText.description: What a screen reader says in place of ImageUrl.

ImagePlacement.description: Where ImageUrl goes. Set it to None to drop the image for one environment without losing the URL from the shared file.

ImageUrl.description: An image for the card — a pipeline's status badge, a team logo, a shield for the environment.

LinkToOtherReports.description: Add a button for every other destination this run reported to — the ReportPortal launch, the Azure DevOps test run — as those reporters posted them to PreceptRunLinks.

MaxFailureMessageLength.description: Longest a failure message may be on the card, in characters.

MaxFailuresListed.description: How many failed tests the card names before it just gives the remaining count. Read by Detailed only — no other variant lists failures.

NotifyOn.description: Which runs are worth a message. Defaults to all of them.

RunUrl.description: Where the card's button goes. Left unset on an Azure DevOps or GitHub Actions agent, the card links to the build that ran the suite — the agent knows its own address, so a test project does not have to be told it.

RunUrlTitle.description: Label on that button. Defaults to naming the detected build — Open build 20260814.3 — and to Open the run when the URL was configured or no build was found.

TimeoutSeconds.description: How long the post may take before it is given up on, in seconds.

Title.description: Heading on the card. Defaults to the test assembly's name.

Variant.description: How the card is laid out. Defaults to Summary.

WebhookUrl.description: The incoming webhook to post to, from the channel's Workflows connector.

TestData.description: Where the test data lives and how it behaves. Bound from the TestData section of precept.json, like any other Precept settings class.

Directory.description: Directory the data files are read from, relative to the test binary unless rooted.

EnvironmentOverlay.description: Load the {file}.{environment}.json overlay beside each file in Files.

Files.description: Data files to load, in increasing order of precedence. Each one is optional, and each is followed by its environment overlay — testdata.json then testdata.staging.json.

LeaseTimeoutMilliseconds.description: How long LeaseAsync``1 waits for a pooled item to come free before giving up. Overridable per pool.

Web.description: Browser automation settings, bound from the Web section of precept.json.

Args.description: Extra command-line arguments for the browser executable, written as one command line — a Chromium flag such as --disable-dev-shm-usage on a container agent, or a proxy, language or feature switch an environment needs. Split by ParseArgs.

AssertionTimeoutMilliseconds.description: How long a web-first assertion — Assert.That(locator).ToBeVisibleAsync() — retries before failing, in milliseconds. Separate from TimeoutMilliseconds on purpose: an action waiting half a minute for an element is patience, an assertion doing the same is a suite that takes half a minute to tell you what is broken.

BaseUrl.description: Base address that relative navigations are resolved against.

Browser.description: Browser engine — chromium, firefox or webkit — or a Chromium channel the machine has installed: chrome or edge, and their -beta, -dev and -canary variants.

CdpEndpoint.description: Connect to a running Chromium over the DevTools protocol — http://localhost:9222. For driving a browser that is already open, which is what a debugging session or a desktop application embedding Chromium offers.

Channel.description: The release channel to launch instead of Playwright's own build — chrome, msedge, or one of their -beta, -dev and -canary variants.

ColorScheme.description: The colour scheme the page's media queries see: light, dark or no-preference. Unset leaves Playwright's default, which is light.

ConsoleLogging.description: How much of what the page writes to the browser console is copied into the test's log. Errors by default.

Device.description: A device from Playwright's registry to emulate — iPhone 15, Pixel 7, iPad Mini landscape. Sets the viewport, user agent, device scale factor and the touch and mobile flags together, which is what makes a page serve its mobile layout.

FailOnConsoleErrors.description: Fail a test whose page wrote an error to the browser console, however well the assertions went.

FailOnPageErrors.description: Fail a test whose page threw an exception nothing caught, however well the assertions went.

Geolocation.description: The position the browser reports, as LATITUDE,LONGITUDE — 51.5074,-0.1278.

HarOnFailure.description: Record the session's network traffic as a HAR file; attached to the test when it fails.

Headless.description: Run without a visible browser window.

HttpCredentials.description: Credentials for HTTP basic authentication, sent to every request the context makes.

Origin.description: Restrict the credentials to this origin, scheme and port included — https://staging.example.com. Unset sends them wherever the page goes, including to a third-party host it happens to load an asset from.

Password.description: The password. Belongs in an environment variable rather than in a settings file.

IgnoreHttpsErrors.description: Continue to a site whose certificate does not validate. Off by default, and worth leaving off where the certificate is real.

InstallBrowsers.description: Whether a browser Playwright has not downloaded is installed rather than failing the run. Auto by default.

Locale.description: The locale the browser reports, as a BCP 47 tag — en-GB, de-DE. Decides the Accept-Language header and the formatting of dates and numbers the page renders.

Permissions.description: Browser permissions granted to every context up front, separated by spaces or commas — geolocation, clipboard-read, notifications.

Proxy.description: The proxy every browser connection goes through — the corporate proxy an agent sits behind, or a recording proxy a suite runs against.

Bypass.description: Hosts to reach directly, comma-separated — localhost,*.internal. Normally where a container or a local stub goes, since a proxy cannot route to the agent's own loopback.

Server.description: The proxy, as http://host:port or socks5://host:port. Nothing else here means anything without it.

Username.description: User name, where the proxy authenticates.

Resolution.description: The viewport as one value: a named resolution — 720p, 900p, 1080p, 1440p, 2160p, or the aliases hd, fhd, qhd, uhd and 4k — or an explicit WIDTHxHEIGHT such as 1366x768. Case-insensitive.

SaveDownloads.description: Save a file the page downloads into the test's artifacts. On by default, and free for a test that never downloads anything.

ScreenshotOnFailure.description: Capture a screenshot when a test fails.

SlowMoMilliseconds.description: Slow each Playwright operation down by this many milliseconds, for debugging.

StorageState.description: A file of cookies and local storage — Playwright's storageState — that every context starts from, so a suite does not sign in once per test.

TimeoutMilliseconds.description: Default timeout for element and navigation waits, in milliseconds.

TimezoneId.description: The time zone the browser reports, as an IANA name — Europe/London, America/New_York. Unset leaves the machine's, with the same drift Locale describes and rather more of it around midnight.

TraceOnFailure.description: Record a Playwright trace; attached to the test when it fails.

UserAgent.description: The user agent every page reports. Unset leaves the browser's own — and a Device's, which is part of what makes the emulation convincing.

VideoOnFailure.description: Record a video of each test; attached when it fails.

ViewportHeight.description: Viewport height in pixels. Ignored when Resolution names one.

ViewportWidth.description: Viewport width in pixels. Ignored when Resolution names one.

WsEndpoint.description: Connect to a browser already running somewhere else, over Playwright's own protocol — ws://grid.internal:3000/. A browser grid, or a vendor's cloud, addresses the suite this way.
